newsitem.title: UK: Surgeon believes Yeltsin has transient condition.
newsitem.headline: Surgeon believes Yeltsin has transient condition.

text.p: Pioneering U.S. heart surgeon Michael DeBakey said on Thursday he believed Russian President Boris Yeltsin's latest illness was a transient condition.
"It's probably flu that he has," DeBakey, a consultant on the major heart surgery performed on Yeltsin last November, told BBC World Service radio.
"There is quite a bit of flu, sort of an epidemic, going on in Moscow and he developed this flu along with other members of the Kremlin, including his family."
DeBakey, speaking from Houston, said Russian doctors felt after taking an x-ray that Yeltsin was "developing a pneumonitis or pneumonia associated with the flu".
"I think this is a transient condition. You know normally people recover from the flu quite well and usually within a week, 10 days, two weeks, it's all over with," he said.
Asked if Yeltsin had recovered from the trauma of the surgery, DeBakey said: "I would say pretty much yes and his heart is functioning now virtually normally."
He said people who underwent such heart surgery were not weakened or made delicate. "Not at all. As a matter of fact they recover normally, they're back to normal condition."

The Kremlin said doctors who examined Yeltsin on Wednesday evening ordered the 65-year-old president back to the Central Clinical Hospital in Moscow where he recuperated after his quintuple bypass operation on November 5.

Yeltsin, who had been looking pale and tired, had already cancelled all appointments since Monday because of what the Kremlin said was a heavy cold. Doctors said the cold was not related to the operation and did not threaten his heart.

"Doctors have stated that the first signs of pneumonia developing have appeared," a Kremlin statement said. "In connection with this, in order to make a better diagnosis and to conduct appropriate treatment, a decision has been taken to take him to the Central Clinical Hospital for several days."

The president, who suffered two heart attacks in 1995 and spent much of last year out of the Kremlin with health problems, had been resting at a country residence outside Moscow because of his illness.

Yeltsin, who played a major role in ending communist rule in 1991 and overseeing economic reforms, has been president since the same year. He fought a tough re-election campaign last year but fell ill just before the decisive round of voting on July 3.
He returned to work in the Kremlin following surgery only on December 23.
